piece.caption: Automate recurring customer communication and appointment booking using Google Gemini Tasks. Stop wasting time on repetitive manual work. Gemini Tasks now allows you to assign specific administrative duties to AI, including calling businesses to check inventory or book service appointments. This feature is now available for free in India within the Gemini app by simply toggling the mode from Chat to Tasks. Remember that for sensitive actions like payments, the AI will always pause and ask for your permission before proceeding. piece.dm_text: Here is how you start using Gemini Tasks: 1. Ensure you are using the latest Gemini app. 2. On the home screen, locate the toggle switch. 3. Change it from 'Chat' to 'Tasks'. 4. Once in Task mode, you can type or speak your request (e.g., 'Call this hardware store and ask for stock'). Note: The AI will ask for permission before sensitive actions like payments. [8] TechCrunch AI — Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/17/google-expands-access-to-gemini-tasks-which-can-help-with-calls-purchases/
Google is expanding the rollout of Tasks, a toggle in Gemini that converts the chatbot into a more active helper.
Unlike Gemini’s Chat, which merely allows users to talk to Google’s AI assistant for informational purposes, Tasks empowers the app to complete basic secretarial functions, deputizing it as a kind of personal assistant.
How, specifically, can you use it? Google says that the app can call businesses and book appointments on users’ behalf; it can also complete purchases for them via Google Pay, and even sign into websites securely if prompted to do so.
In a blog post , Josh Woodword, VP of Gemini, claims to have recently used the feature to call local car dealerships to schedule a service appointment for his family’s minivan. He says he also used it to analyze his electrical bill.
Tasks was initially launched to select testers back in May as Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agentic helper, and was expanded to U.S. subscribers of its Google AI Ultra tier. Gemini Spark eventually became “Task Mode.” Google is now making the feature available for free to hundreds of millions of people who are using the company’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.
Getting the function up and running is easy. Users merely flip a toggle within the app from Chat to Tasks, which enables the feature. Users can also send texts to Gemini or call the app to give it commands.

Emma Roth is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO. Google is rebranding its Spark AI agent as “Tasks” and making it free to use. The feature, which is powered by Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model, can do things like create meal plans, manage your calendar, and dig through your emails to find recurring expenses you might not need.
Users in the US will get access to a few other features, including the ability for the AI agent to call businesses to compare product pricing and check inventory, purchase items with Google Pay, and sign into accounts that support Google Password Manager. US users can also assign Gemini tasks by emailing gemini@google.com or texting it.
Google first introduced its Spark AI agent in May , but it was only available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. The launch of tasks in Gemini brings Spark’s capabilities to all users in the US, Canada, Japan, Korea, Australia, and India. You can find tasks by opening Gemini and changing the toggle on the homepage from “Chat” to “Tasks.”
Tasks in Gemini is just one of the many agentic AI features that have emerged over the past year, including Claude Duet, OpenAI’s Dots , and Meta’s Muse . Google says Gemini will perform tasks in a “hardware-isolated virtual machine that’s dedicated to your account and never shared with other users.” You can also provide instructions for Gemini while it completes tasks. When performing more sensitive tasks, like purchasing an item, it will stop working and ask for your permission before following through.

[70] Inc42 — Google Begins Rolling Out Personal AI Assistant, Tasks, In India
URL: https://inc42.com/buzz/google-begins-rolling-out-personal-ai-assistant-tasks-in-india/
Google Begins Rolling Out Personal AI Assistant, Tasks, In India --> tag --> Skip to content Google Begins Rolling Out Personal AI Assistant, Tasks, In India --> SHARE Share on Facebook
SUMMARY The new feature will enable users to assign tasks to the AI assistant, including making calls, booking appointments, comparing products, making payments and completing purchases
From Meta’s Muse to OpenAI’s Dots, a growing wave of big tech giants are rolling out personal AI assistants to capture the masses and automate daily chores
India’s inclusion in the initial rollout gives Google a large market to test consumer adoption of the personal AI assistant. The service comes bundled for free with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model
Added to Saved Stories in Login VIEW SAVED STORIES
Big tech giant Google has begun rolling out its new agentic AI assistant Tasks, formerly Gemini Sparks, to users in India.
In a blogpost , Josh Woodward, the vice-president of Google Labs and the Gemini app, said that the new feature will enable users to assign tasks to the AI assistant, including making calls, booking appointments, comparing products and completing purchases.
The service comes bundled for free with Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.
“Starting now, this update is rolling out free of charge for hundreds of millions of people across the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, using our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model,” said Woodward.
It is pertinent to note that Tasks was reportedly initially launched to select testers back in May as Gemini Spark, an agentic AI helper. It was subsequently expanded to the US-based subscribers of the Google AI Ultra tier. Google is now rolling out this feature for free in six markets.
Unlike Gemini’s Chat that only generates responses to a user’s queries, Tasks goes one step further and enables the chatbot to perform basic functions. With the rollout, Google could be looking to expand the role of AI assistants beyond answering questions to embedding them in daily life.
In his blog post, Woodward noted that Gemini can draw on information already available within Google services, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, files and payment cards, to carry out tasks on a user’s behalf. With Tasks, he also said that Gemini can call businesses, wait through hold periods, identify available appointment slots and add bookings to a user’s calendar.
Under the hood, Gemini uses the agent payments protocol (AP2) to enable Tasks to make purchases online. Going forward, the big tech giant said that it plans to integrate the universal commerce protocol (UCP) into Gemini to further streamline the checkout experience.
Google also said that it is working with American Express, Mastercard and Visa to enable tokenised card transactions via Tasks. However, the big tech juggernaut did not specify whether partnerships extend to India too.
That said, India’s inclusion in the initial rollout gives Google a large market to test consumer adoption of the personal AI assistant feature. To further scale the rollout, Google has also invited app developers to join its Connected Apps Platform, which could pave the way for Indian consumer, fintech, travel tech and foodtech brands to build task-based third-party integrations with the assistant.
These features could make Gemini Tasks a channel for online shopping, bill payments and routine purchases. However, adoption will depend on the availability of supported merchants, payment methods and third-party apps in the country. There appears to be no clarity on this front.
The launch is part of a broader wave of big tech giants rolling out personal AI assistants to capture the masses. In September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg showcased the company’s new offering called Muse, which allows an AI agent to send emails, fill forms, make plans and even make purchases autonomously.
Prior to this, OpenAI also introduced Dots that can draft board meeting decks, conduct background research, and handle multi-step project management. xAI has also been developing Grok Bot, which sees cleaning up sales records and processing invoices as potential uses for agents.
Microsoft is also pursuing agents, built on OpenClaw, which can function as digital teammates. Back home, Emergent, better known for its vibe-coding platform, launched Wingman, an autonomous agent that handles routine actions and seeks approval before taking bigger steps.
